newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down 1.5 pct as electronics fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down 1.5 pct as electronics fall.

text.p: Persistent profit-taking in the recent bellwether electronics sector pulled Taiwan share prices sharply lower on Wednesday, but brokers said they expected the correction to be short-lived.
The index finished down 125.98 points or 1.50 percent at 8,267.00, off an intraday high of 8,408.22.
Turnover was a moderately active T$122.7 billion.
Electronics were down a striking 2.97 percent, with leading chipmakers Taiwan Semiconductor and United Microelectronics down T$4 and T$3.5, respectively, to T$130.5 and T$86.

Brokers also attributed the fall in part to new concern over ongoing constitutional reforms as a tentative agreement between Taiwan's two major political parties showed signs of failing -- though this was unlikely to have fundamental impact.
"Concern over constitutional reform should be only an excuse for the index fall, as the reform should not affect our economy and markets much," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.

China-concept shares -- Taiwan firms with active or planned investments in the communist mainland -- also encountered heavy profit-taking, with Liton Electronic down by the daily seven percent limit to T$98.
China-concepts had surged last week -- a coattail benefit reflecting big gains by Hong Kong's China-linked shares ahead of the British colony's July 1 handover to Beijing.
Brokers cautioned that Taiwan's China-concept shares were showing acute sensitivity to Beijing-Hong Kong politics.
"Recent reports that the Chinese communists intend to cool down the China-linked shares' surges in Hong Kong have had a negative impact on China-concept shares here," Yang said.
Warrant-eligible shares rose to support the market, with Pacific Wire and Cable up 40 cents to T$41.3 and Formosa Plastics up 50 cents to T$76.
